q: A screen lists a user's notes with no limit. What happens as the user writes more notes?
o: The query gets an index error
The cost of each open grows with the notes
why: You pay one read per document returned, so an unlimited query costs more as data grows.

q: where on ownerId plus orderBy on createdAt fails in production with a link in the error. What do you do?
o: Create the composite index from the link
why: Filtering and sorting on two fields needs a composite index, which you create yourself.

q: A shared board shows 20 notes with author names and opens very often. Best design?
o: Store all notes in one document
Join notes and users in a query
why: Copying a rarely changing name makes the board one query; the cost is extra writes when a name changes.

q: Ana renames herself and has 300 notes with authorName copied. What is the cost?
why: Each copy is its own field in its own document, so each must be rewritten.

q: You call setDoc on users/{uid} with only { name }. The photo field disappears. Why?
why: Without { merge: true }, setDoc replaces the document. Use merge or updateDoc.

q: To show page 50 of notes cheaply, you should use …
why: offset still reads and bills every skipped document; a cursor starts right after the last one.

q: A live listener costs reads only once, when it starts.
why: It costs one read per document in the first result, then one read for each added, changed or removed document.

q: A note's photo should go in Cloud Storage, with only its path saved in Firestore.
why: A document can be at most 1 MiB and every read would download the photo; files belong in Cloud Storage.
